t: Đông Sơn is an archaeological culture named after a village in Thanh Hóa province, Vietnam, where bronze drums were first excavated in 1924; it centred on the Red River Delta.
Its people farmed rice, kept water buffalo and pigs, fished and sailed long dugout canoes, and cast bronze drums decorated with scenes of their world.
Who the Đông Sơn people were is debated: some link them to the Vietic ancestors of the Vietnamese, others see several peoples who shared one trading culture.
dyk: The Cổ Loa drum weighs 72 kilograms, and casting it would have required the smelting of between 1 and 7 tonnes of copper ore.
ev: The Đông Sơn culture emerges from the Gò Mun culture in northern Vietnam
The Chinese text Shiben gives the first literary mention of bronze drums
After the defeat of the Trưng sisters and the Han general Ma Yuan’s conquest of the Red River Plain, the bronze drum culture disappears
Scattered Đông Sơn bronzes are said to have been found again under the Lý dynasty
The Austrian archaeologist Franz Heger, creator of a classification of bronze drums, turns to the drums
A fisherman, Nguyễn Văn Lắm, reports bronze finds to the École française d’Extrême-Orient, and excavations begin at Đông Sơn village
Finds in Isan, Thailand, show that bronze casting began in Southeast Asia first or developed there independently of China

f.homeland: Northern Vietnam, centred on the Red River Delta; named after the village of Đông Sơn in Thanh Hóa province; related finds in Laos, Malaysia and the Chinese provinces of Yunnan, Guangxi and Fujian; sites include Đông Sơn and Núi Nấp.
f.period: c. 1000 BCE – 1st century CE; it grew out of the Gò Mun culture and marks the culmination of the Bronze Age and the opening of the Iron Age; its bronze drum culture disappears after the Han conquest of the Red River Plain.
f.known: Heger I bronze kettledrums decorated with a sun, frogs, warships and feather-headdressed warriors; lost-wax bronze casting; rice farming; water buffalo and pigs; fishing and sailing in long dugout canoes; bronze daggers
f.sources: Excavations at Đông Sơn village from 1924; the bronze drums and analyses of their metal; early Chinese texts such as the Shiben; ancient DNA and skull studies; the history of the Vietic languages.
